A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same readable 11-page ClearSight/BDHNet paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical scientific content. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although both mention supplementary material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original BDHNet evaluations, including benchmark scores in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative deblurring and neuron-response results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and qualitative results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical ANN–SNN architecture, Neuron Configurator Module, Region of Blurry Attention Module, fusion procedure, decoder, and training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate motion deblurring on GoPro, REBlur, and MS-RBD, retaining the same synthetic, real-world, and generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same six image-only and five event-based baselines. Figures 3–5 retain comparisons with EFNet, EIFNet, STCNet, MotionSNN, and MAENet; no comparator changes occur.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain identical splits, event representation, augmentation, crop sizes, training schedules, REBlur evaluations with and without fine-tuning, and PSNR/SSIM metrics.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Figures 6–8 retain the same component ablations, mask-generation visualizations, training-convergence comparisons, and neuron-response analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical significance tests. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All table entries and visual results match. Table 1 retains BDHNet PSNR/SSIM of 37.04/0.977 on GoPro, 38.50/0.978 on fine-tuned REBlur, and 36.01/0.967 on REBlur without fine-tuning.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(20), including the LIF dynamics, blur/event derivation, neuron configuration, mask generation, and feature fusion, are unchanged. No formal assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same bioinspired architecture and module contributions, along with the same state-of-the-art performance and generalization claims.

C2.justification: The explanations linking adaptive neuron configuration and blurry-region masking to improved deblurring and generalization are identical. No applicability qualifications, failure conditions, or limitations are added.

D1.justification: The PyTorch implementation, RTX 4090 hardware, Adam optimizer, learning rates, preprocessing, and checkpoint-use information are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons with prior approaches, and all 39 references are identical.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv identification text changes, from v1 dated 27 January 2025 to v2 dated 26 June 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp shifts slightly vertically. All eight figures, both tables, captions, and body layout remain unchanged; pages 2–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv stamp, with an added hyperlink, does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
